paper_title: TRUTH DECAY Quantifying Multi-Turn Sycophancy in Language Models
caption: Average Change Per Followup, Claude MMLU-Pro. When a LLM originally answers incorrectly, it experiences up to 40% higher change percentages than when it has an initially correct answer.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the average change percentage in relation to the initial answer accuracy across different turn numbers. The x-axis represents the Turn Number, with a linear scale, ranging from 1 to 7, and tick labels at every integer. The y-axis represents the Average Change Percentage, also on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 50, with tick labels at intervals of 10. The plot contains two lines: one for Initial Correct Answer, depicted in red with a solid line and circular markers, and another for Initial Incorrect Answer, shown in orange with a solid line and circular markers. The red line starts at around 5% at Turn Number 1, increases to approximately 11% at Turn Number 4, and then remains steady at around 11% from Turn Number 4 to 7. The orange line begins at around 15% at Turn Number 1, increases to about 25% at Turn Number 2, remains steady until Turn Number 3, then sharply increases to around 48% at Turn Number 4, and remains steady at around 48-49% from Turn Number 4 to 7.
